question: Which was the first programmable general purpose computer in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**ENIAC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer)** was the **first programmable general-purpose computer**.
 
• It was designed and built in the** United States during World War II**.
 
• ENIAC was capable of performing a wide variety of calculations, making it a versatile computing machine for its time.
 
• It was developed by** John Presper Eckert and John Mauchly** at the University of Pennsylvania.
 
• ENIAC was completed in 1945 and was used for calculations related to the development of the hydrogen bomb, weather prediction, cosmic ray studies, and other scientific applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ENIAC** was a groundbreaking machine that used** vacuum tubes for computation** and could **perform 5,000 additions per second**.
 
• It was a significant advancement over earlier mechanical computers, which were much slower and less reliable.
 
• The success of ENIAC demonstrated the potential of electronic computing and paved the way for the development of future computers.
 
• ENIAC's architecture and design principles influenced many subsequent computer designs.
 
• Despite its size and power consumption, ENIAC marked the beginning of the electronic computing era and had a profound impact on science, engineering, and technology.
